properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-26, from the same brainstorm — this one is the instrument his framing implies rather than an idea he stated.

**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.**

═══ THE SIGNAL NOBODY IS COLLECTING ═══

Every existing measurement looks at what a session **did** with reflow2: `surface_usage.py` counts calls, `cap:skill-loads-are-counted` counts loads, `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` asks where to put the log. All of them are blind to the same thing —

**the work a session performed BY HAND that reflow2 already serves.**

That is the negative space, and it is a far stronger signal than absence-of-a-call, because it carries INTENT. A tool never called might be young, might have no use case yet, might be unfindable — `dec:bl-155` lists exactly those three explanations and says it *"cannot tell unused from unreachable."* **Hand-rolled work discriminates between them.** A session that wrote a script to do X proves someone wanted X, at a moment, badly enough to build it. That is not weak evidence of a retrieval failure; it is close to proof.

═══ IT IS ALREADY REPRODUCING, INCLUDING TODAY ═══

- **2026-08-26 (this session).** Comparing the allocation layer against the artifact layer — 212 capabilities, 59 agree / 23 disagree / 130 no evidence — was done with a hand-written Python script over the export. It found the session's central result. **No reflow2 tool does it:** `reconcile_artifacts` compares design against DISK, `compare_designs` compares design against DESIGN, and neither compares two layers of ONE design. Here the hand-rolled work names a MISSING tool.
- **2026-08-20.** *"does my declared decomposition match the real coupling?"* — again a hand-written script, again the session's finding.
- **The v0.19.0-v0.31.0 release cuts.** A ~40-line JSON-RPC driver written and rewritten to export through a specific binary, eventually promoted into `tools/`. Hand-rolled work that became kit — the same signal, acted on late.

⭐ Note the two different diagnoses the same signal produces: sometimes the tool is MISSING, sometimes it exists and was not FOUND. The instrument does not have to tell them apart — a human reading the list can, and either answer is worth having.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) A transcript-side detector: scripts written during a session, matched against the served surface.** Bash heredocs, `python3 - <<`, one-off files under a scratchpad. ⚠️ Counter: it reads TRANSCRIPTS, which is a different privacy posture from anything reflow2 does today — `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` says usage telemetry carries the verb and never the object, and a script's SOURCE is design content. The instrument would have to report the SHAPE of the work and never its content, which may not be extractable.

**(b) Ask the agent, at session end, one question: "what did you do by hand that reflow2 should have done?"** Costs one prompt, no new surveillance, and both prior findings surfaced this way — by asking an agent. ⚠️ Counter: self-report, which is precisely the evidence `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` had to fall back on twice and complains about both times. An agent that did not notice a tool existed is the same agent being asked whether one should have.

**(c) Do nothing here, and treat hand-rolled work as a FRICTION report.** `report-friction` already exists for "reflow2 got in my way", and "I had to write this myself" is that. ⚠️ Counter: friction reporting is voluntary and fires on a wall, not on a quiet detour. Nobody files friction for a script that worked.

**(d) Narrow it to the highest-value case: hand-written analysis over the EXPORTED design file.** Much easier to spot than arbitrary scripting, and both 2026 findings are exactly this shape. ⚠️ Counter: a narrow instrument measures a narrow thing, and it would have missed the release-cut driver entirely.

═══ WHAT IT WOULD BE WORTH ═══

If it works it feeds all three open questions at once: it tells `dec:bl-155` which of its 40 are unreachable rather than unused; it hands `dec:idea-a-problem-in-the-users-words-should-retrieve-the-tool-that-answers-it` real question→tool pairs from the tail rather than the head; and it is a layer-④ instrument that does not depend on the agent volunteering anything.

🛑 **AND THE HONEST OBJECTION TO ALL FOUR:** the two findings this node rests on were both found by an agent noticing and saying so, unprompted. It is entirely possible the mechanism does not need building, only asking — and that (b), the cheapest option, is also the one already working.
properties.name: OPEN — can reflow2 detect work a session did BY HAND that a served tool already does, and is that the missing instrument?
properties.rationale:
Recorded separately from the other two because it is a buildable instrument rather than a frame or a retrieval question, and could be attempted without settling either. It is also the only one of the three that produces EVIDENCE rather than consuming it, which is why the closing objection matters: if asking already works, building is over-engineering, and that is the failure mode this project watches for by name.

Written down at all because the signal reproduced three times across five weeks and nothing in the design names it. Two of the three instances found the session's central result, so the pattern is not incidental.
